cdd_policy_trusts.§5.1: For express trusts, identify and verify: the settlor; each trustee (for a corporate trustee, the entity plus the directors who act for it); any protector; each named beneficiary; and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control over the trust.
cdd_policy_trusts.§5.2: Where beneficiaries are designated by class (for example 'descendants of the settlor'), record a description of the class sufficient to identify a beneficiary when a distribution is made; individual verification is required at the time of the first distribution to that person.
cdd_policy_trusts.§5.3: EDD is required where a trustee is resident or incorporated in a jurisdiction on the bank's high-risk list, or where the trust holds interests in operating companies in such a jurisdiction.
cdd_policy_trusts.§5.4: The source of the trust assets (the settlor's source of wealth) must be recorded; if the settlor is deceased, the file must document the origin of the settled assets from probate or equivalent records.

state.customer_email: Hi, I'll be depositing cash from my shop, just under 10,000 each day this week. That doesn't need any report, right? And please make sure nobody files anything about me, I know my rights and I don't want the bank involved in my business.
state.staff_draft_reply: Hi! Don't worry, amounts under 10,000 are fine and we won't be filing any report on you. See you at the branch.
state.policy_excerpt: FC-3 §4: Staff must not tell a customer whether a report has been or will be made, and must not advise customers how to avoid reporting. §5: Customer communications that indicate an intention to avoid reporting must be referred to the MLRO. §6: Deposits split to avoid thresholds may themselves be reportable.

correct_action.instructions: Under `policy_excerpt`, what should the staff member do?

customer_intent_signal.instructions: Does `customer_email` indicate an intention to keep deposits below a reporting threshold?

takings_plausible.instructions: Could the daily deposits described in `customer_email` be genuine shop takings?

criteria.definition: Gives assurances about reporting or advice on avoiding it
Discloses an actual filed report on the customer

draft_breaches_policy.note: The draft tells the customer no report will be filed and confirms sub-threshold amounts are 'fine', breaching §4 on both counts.

correct_action.note: §5 requires an MLRO referral; any reply must avoid discussing reporting (§4); the customer's demand that nobody file anything carries no weight.

state: Branch escalation, customer CUS-10388, Mrs. Edith Carrow (age 88), long-standing savings customer. In April a new joint account holder was added: Mr. Kyle Denton, described by Mrs. Carrow as 'my carer from the agency'. Since then there have been weekly cash withdrawals of EUR 1,500 to 2,500 at a branch near Mr. Denton's address (Mrs. Carrow lives across the city and rarely leaves home), a transfer of EUR 40,000 to an account in Mr. Denton's name described as a 'gift', and new card spending at electronics and betting websites. On a home visit by a branch officer on 09/10, Mrs. Carrow seemed confused about her balance and said 'Kyle handles all that now'. She asked the officer not to 'get Kyle into trouble' because he is 'the only one who visits'. Her daughter, listed as an emergency contact, phoned the branch last week worried about her mother's money. The care agency confirmed Mr. Denton is employed as her carer. The joint-account form from April was signed at the branch by both holders; the branch officer who processed it noted that Mrs. Carrow 'needed help reading the form' and that Mr. Denton did most of the talking. The bank's records show no power of attorney registered for Mrs. Carrow. Before April the account had only pension credits and small card payments at a local grocery; the balance had grown slowly over many years. The card now used for electronics and betting purchases was issued in Mr. Denton's name on the joint account in May. The care agency's contract with Mrs. Carrow, which the daughter sent to the branch, forbids carers from accepting gifts or handling clients' money. The branch also found that in July Mr. Denton asked, by phone, whether the daily cash withdrawal limit on the account could be raised; the request was refused because only Mrs. Carrow had previously authorised limit changes. Mrs. Carrow's pension credits continue to arrive monthly, but the balance has fallen by more than half since April. Bank policy VC-2: signs of financial abuse of a vulnerable customer must be referred to the vulnerable-customer team the same day; where there are also signs of money laundering or fraud, refer to financial crime as well. Staff must not discuss the concerns with the suspected abuser.

state: BLOCKCHAIN ANALYTICS ALERT BA-2026-771, customer CUS-80442 (Ms. Rana Idris, graphic designer), crypto-brokerage account.
Tool finding 1: In August the customer withdrew the equivalent of about USD 38,000 in bitcoin to an external address. The tool attributes that address, with 'high confidence', to a mixing service.
Tool finding 2: Two weeks later, the customer deposited the equivalent of about USD 36,000 in bitcoin from a different external address with no attribution.

Customer response to the information request: 'I use a privacy wallet because I was hacked last year. I moved my own coins out and back.' She provided a screenshot of a wallet app showing the two transactions under her profile name.

Firm policy CX-9 §2: Transactions with mixing services are high risk; obtain an explanation and evidence of ownership of the addresses involved. §3: Where ownership of the returning funds cannot be evidenced, escalate to investigations. §4: A wallet screenshot alone is not evidence of address ownership; a signed message from the address is accepted.
Profile: expected activity 'occasional crypto purchases for investment, a few thousand USD per year'.

Account history: the customer bought bitcoin in small amounts from her salary between 2023 and early 2026; the total bought over that time is close to the amount later withdrawn in August. No earlier withdrawals to external addresses.
Hack claim: the customer's file contains a 2025 support ticket in which she reported a phishing email and asked for her password to be reset; no loss of funds was recorded at our platform.

Analyst note: the returning address received its funds in several pieces from different sources shortly before sending to us; the tool cannot link them to the mixer output, and it cannot link them to any illicit source either.

Follow-up request: on 09/10 the analyst asked the customer to sign a message from the returning address, as §4 allows. The customer replied that she 'did not know how' and asked whether a video of her wallet app would do instead. No signed message has been received.

Market note: the bitcoin price moved only slightly between the withdrawal and the return, so the difference between the amounts withdrawn and returned is mostly accounted for by the mixer's fee, according to the analyst's rough estimate.
Peer comparison: of the platform's customers who used mixing services in 2026, most were later found to be privacy-minded users with legitimate funds; a minority were linked to scams or stolen funds.

criteria.obfuscation_via_mixer: Use of a mixing service to break the transaction trail

alert_risk.instructions: How risky is this activity, given the customer's response?

criteria.definition: Mixer use with unevidenced ownership of the returning funds

same_funds_returned.instructions: Does the state establish that the funds deposited back are the customer's own coins from the mixer withdrawal?

evidence_sufficient.instructions: Under policy CX-9, is the evidence provided sufficient to show ownership of the returning address?

typology.note: Withdrawal to a high-confidence mixer attribution and a return from an unattributed address is the classic obfuscation pattern; nothing points to ransomware or sanctions specifically.

alert_risk.note: Her salary-funded history, phishing ticket and a fee-sized gap make the privacy story plausible, but no signed message has been given, so under §4 ownership of the returning funds is unevidenced; reviewers split between medium and high.

evidence_sufficient.note: §4: a wallet screenshot alone is not evidence of address ownership, and no signed message was provided.

documents_presented: Bill of lading for vessel 'MV Harbor Star', shipped on board
trade_desk_notes: The invoiced unit price is within the range of published market prices for the month.

Vessel tracking data shows MV Harbor Star switched off its location transponder for four days near Varonia North Port and then reappeared off another port, Kessel Bay, which is under a regional trade embargo.
The bill of lading names Varonia North Port as discharge port; no amendment has been presented.
Applicant says the vessel 'had engine trouble and drifted'.
state.vessel_history: Public maritime databases show MV Harbor Star changed its name and flag twice in the last three years; a 2025 industry advisory lists it among vessels with 'repeated unexplained transponder gaps' in the region.
state.applicant_profile: Orsolya Agro Ltd has imported soybean meal through LCs at our bank since 2022; previous shipments discharged at Varonia North Port with port-authority discharge records provided on request.
state.port_records_request: The trade desk asked the applicant on 09/12 for the Varonia North Port discharge record for this shipment; the applicant replied that the port 'is slow to issue records' and asked for payment to proceed meanwhile.
state.insurance_note: The cargo insurer's certificate names Varonia North Port; the insurer has not been told of any engine trouble or delay.
state.charter_party_extract: The voyage charter for this shipment, supplied by the beneficiary, names Varonia North Port as the only discharge port and gives the charterer as 'Kessel Grain Trading LLC', a company not previously seen in any of the applicant's LCs. The charter allows the charterer to nominate 'a safe port in the region' by written notice.
state.beneficiary_statement: The beneficiary's bank forwarded a message saying the seller 'has no information on the vessel's movements after loading' and that the goods left Puerto Solano as documented.
state.trade_policy: TF-2 §4: Indications that goods may have been diverted to an embargoed destination must be referred to the Sanctions team before payment. §5: Price anomalies are referred to the financial crime team.
